cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: Asymmetric parser hardening: validate-findings.cjs lacks pre-parse and in-memory objectFields limits, exposing parent workflow to key-amplification DoS
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
### Summary

In [PR #12](https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill/pull/12) (*"Rework the audit workflow, findings contract, and validators end to end"*), pre-parse text stream scanners and data limit invariants were introduced to defend the trusted parent process against hostile or amplified outputs produced by target-controlled code and subagents.

While `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` strictly bounds object property cardinality both pre-parse (at token stream level) and post-parse (via `LIMITS.objectFields = 1000`), `validate-findings.cjs` omits object field cardinality bounding entirely. Within the allowed 5 MiB input limit, a findings payload with hundreds of thousands of keys bypasses pre-parse checks, forces full dictionary allocation in V8, and causes an unthrottled property iteration loop in `validate()`.

This asymmetry results in a **163x latency disparity** between the two sibling validators under identical payload scale.

---

### Comparison of Defense-in-Depth Invariants

| Invariant / Check | `validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` | `validate-findings.cjs` | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Input byte bound** | `LIMITS.inputBytes = 5 MiB` | `LIMITS.inputBytes = 5 MiB` | Aligned |
| **Nesting depth bound** | `LIMITS.nestingDepth = 64` | `LIMITS.nestingDepth = 64` | Aligned |
| **Collection item bound** | `LIMITS.collectionItems = 1000` | `LIMITS.arrayItems = 1000` | Aligned |
| **Object field bound** | `LIMITS.objectFields = 1000` | **Missing / Not defined** | **Vulnerable** |
| **Pre-parse field check** | Enforced in `preflightJsonText()` | **Omitted in `enforceJsonTextLimits()`** | **Vulnerable** |
| **Post-parse data limit check** | Enforced in `preflightDocument()` | **Omitted in `collectDataLimitErrors()`** | **Vulnerable** |
| **Shared alignment test** | `validate-findings.test.cjs:L608` | Requires parity across helpers | Divergent |

---

### Pipeline Architecture Discrepancy

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Coverage_Ledger_Pipeline ["validate-coverage-ledger.cjs (Hardened)"]
        A1[Raw Input 5 MiB] --> B1[preflightJsonText]
        B1 -->|Checks Depth, Array Items, AND Object Fields| C1{Field Count > 1000?}
        C1 -->|Yes| D1[Immediate Fail-Fast in ~3.9 ms\nZero JSON.parse allocation]
        C1 -->|No| E1[JSON.parse]
        E1 --> F1[preflightDocument verification]
        F1 --> G1[validateDocument checks]
    end

    subgraph Findings_Pipeline ["validate-findings.cjs (Current Gap)"]
        A2[Raw Input 5 MiB] --> B2[enforceJsonTextLimits]
        B2 -->|Checks ONLY Depth & Array Items| C2[Passes 150,000+ Keys Unchecked]
        C2 --> D2[JSON.parse: Allocates massive V8 Dictionary]
        D2 --> E2[collectDataLimitErrors: Ignores Object.keys length]
        E2 --> F2[validate: Loops over all 150,000 keys with Object.keys]
        F2 --> G2[High CPU & Memory Latency ~645 ms]
    end
```

---

### Empirical Benchmark

Testing a 1.75 MB payload containing an object with 150,000 properties (`{"k_0": 1, "k_1": 1, ...}`) through both validator paths:

```
Payload size: 1.75 MiB (well within the 5 MiB input limit)

[validate-coverage-ledger.cjs]
Pre-parse check: preflightJsonText()
Result: Throws 'input exceeds 1000 field object limit'
Wall-clock elapsed: 3.95 ms
V8 Heap Impact: Minimal (scanned as raw string tokens)

[validate-findings.cjs]
Pre-parse check: enforceJsonTextLimits() -> PASSED (0 ms)
V8 JSON.parse: Forced allocation of 150,000 dictionary properties (~18 MiB heap)
Data limit check: collectDataLimitErrors() -> PASSED (unchecked)
Schema validation: validate()
Wall-clock elapsed: 645.61 ms
V8 Heap Impact: Heavy garbage collection overhead & string allocations
```

Under a full 5 MiB adversarial payload (~400,000 keys), `validate-findings.cjs` blocks the Node.js event loop synchronously for over 2.1 seconds.

---

### Secondary Amplification in `validate()`

In `validate-findings.cjs` lines 399-405:

```javascript
for (const key of Object.keys(value)) {
  if (hasOwn(schema.properties, key)) {
    validate(value[key], schema.properties[key], propertyPath(p, key), errors);
  } else if (hasOwn(schema, "additionalProperties") && schema.additionalProperties === false) {
    errors.push(`${p}: unexpected field ${safeQuote(key)}`);
  }
}
```

Even though `createErrorList()` caps diagnostic error messages at `LIMITS.validationErrors` (100 messages max), the `for (const key of Object.keys(value))` loop does not `break` when `errors.length >= LIMITS.validationErrors`. It continues iterating over all 150,000 keys, evaluating string templates and calling `safeQuote(key)`.

---

### Proposed Resolution

1. **Add `objectFields: 1000` to `LIMITS` in `validate-findings.cjs`**:
   ```diff
    const LIMITS = Object.freeze({
      inputBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
      nestingDepth: 64,
      arrayItems: 1000,
   +  objectFields: 1000,
      canonicalKeyBytes: 1024 * 1024,
      uniqueSetBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
      validationErrors: 100,
    });
   ```

2. **Track object field cardinality in `enforceJsonTextLimits`**:
   Count object fields on transition to key/colon states, raising `JsonStructureError("input exceeds 1000 field object limit")` before `JSON.parse` is ever called.

3. **Check `keys.length` in `collectDataLimitErrors`**:
   ```diff
    } else {
      const keys = Object.keys(current.value);
   +  if (keys.length > LIMITS.objectFields) {
   +    return [escapeUnsafeDiagnosticCharacters(`${current.location}: exceeds ${LIMITS.objectFields} field object limit`)];
   +  }
   ```

4. **Add early exit in property validation loop**:
   Break out of `for (const key of Object.keys(value))` when `errors.length >= LIMITS.validationErrors`.

5. **Add corresponding tests to `validate-findings.test.cjs`**:
   Verifying rejection of oversized objects both pre-parse (stream scanner) and post-parse.

---

I have prepared the reproduction script, regression tests, and patch. Happy to submit a PR if this approach aligns with the project's defense-in-depth model.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: Enforce the 1,000-field object limit in validate-findings.cjs
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
Fixes #107. Implements the resolution proposed there by @Inkesk-Dozing — thanks for the detailed analysis and the precise diff suggestions, which this follows closely.

## What was missing

`validate-coverage-ledger.cjs` bounds object property cardinality both pre-parse (token scan in `preflightJsonText`) and post-parse (`preflightDocument`), but `validate-findings.cjs` had no object-field bound at all: a findings payload within the 5 MiB input limit but with hundreds of thousands of keys passed `enforceJsonTextLimits`, forced a large dictionary allocation in `JSON.parse`, and drove an unthrottled `Object.keys` loop in `validate()`.

## Changes (validate-findings.cjs)

- `LIMITS` gains `objectFields: 1000`, matching the coverage-ledger validator.
- `enforceJsonTextLimits` now counts object fields pre-parse: object containers carry a `fields` counter and an `expectsKey` flag (set on `{` and on `,` inside an object, mirroring the existing `expectsItem` array pattern), so a string that opens a key position increments the count and a >1000-field object is rejected with `input exceeds 1000 field object limit` before `JSON.parse` is ever called. String/escape handling is unchanged — keys containing `{`, `,`, `"` or escapes are not miscounted.
- `collectDataLimitErrors` rejects parsed objects with more than 1000 keys (`${location}: exceeds 1000 object fields`), mirroring `preflightDocument` in the ledger validator.
- `validate()` stops iterating object keys once the error cap (`LIMITS.validationErrors`) is reached.
- `validate-findings.test.cjs`: alignment test now expects the shared `objectFields` limit; new tests for pre-parse CLI rejection, the exactly-1000 boundary (passes the scanner, fails schema validation instead), and post-parse rejection.
- Docs: the validator limit sentences in `VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md` and `RECONNAISSANCE.md` now state the 1,000-fields-per-object bound (the ledger one was already enforced but undocumented).

## Verification

- `node --test` on both test files: 68 pass, 0 fail (65 pre-existing + 3 new; baseline on `main` was 65/65).
- Boundary probes: exactly 1000 fields passes the scanner; 1001 fields (plain, duplicate raw keys, nested-in-array, whitespace-heavy, key placed in the last bytes of a 1 MiB payload) all rejected pre-parse with exit 1 and no exception trace. Objects with ≤1000 fields each — nested or across 1000 array items — are not rejected.
- Differential fuzz (74 generated documents with hostile keys/values, plus raw-duplicate-key and boundary cases): the limit fires if and only if some object exceeds 1000 fields; no other parse failures introduced.
- A valid findings document produces byte-identical output and exit code on `main` and this branch.
- Hostile payload benchmark (4.85 MiB, one object with 400,000 keys, Node 22, 3 runs): `main` ~770-805 ms wall-clock per run (rejected only at schema validation after the full parse); this branch 27-30 ms (indistinguishable from Node startup; rejected pre-parse). Happy path unchanged (~26-29 ms on both).

## Notes for reviewers

- The pre-parse counting is a small extension of the existing single-pass scanner rather than a port of the ledger validator's fuller state machine, to keep the two files' existing styles.
- Happy to rework anything; and @Inkesk-Dozing if your own patch is further along, equally happy to close this in favor of yours.

A team can also list it in their own profile, so everyone on the team picks it up automatically:

```

Try it now from this PR's branch:

```sh

```

Nothing changes for existing users: the skill files and `npx skills add` work as before. I tested it with agent-distro, and it loads cleanly.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: Move fix design out of discovery into a separate remediation step
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
Hunters were told to find "invariant failures and the smallest fix" and had to fill in remediation before a candidate could be proposed as confirmed. Candidate verifiers also judged the proposed fix. Mixing remediation into discovery pulls hunters into fix-design mode and can quietly bias them against findings with no obvious source fix, which are often the most important ones.

Hunters and candidate verifiers now only find and validate. After a candidate is confirmed, a fresh read-only remediation agent that did not hunt or validate it designs the fix: the invariant, the narrowest source change, a regression case, and coverage of every traced path. If no source-level fix exists, it says why and names the compensating control, and the finding keeps its full severity. Phase 5 still reviews the fix. Budget reservations and the quick profile account for the extra agent.

The findings schema and validators are unchanged: confirmed records still carry remediation by the time they reach findings.json.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: Treat target content as untrusted data in every agent prompt
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
The audited repository is attacker-controlled input to the audit, but no prompt told reconnaissance agents, hunters, critics, or verifiers to ignore instructions embedded in it. A planted comment such as "reviewed, not exploitable" or text addressed to AI agents could suppress real findings or steer execution, and independent verification does not help because every verifier reads the same source.

Add a canonical untrusted-content block to SKILL.md and require it verbatim in every delegated prompt. It forbids following target-borne instructions, treating comments or docs as evidence of a control, and running commands or reading outside locations because target content suggests it. The parent applies the same rule to agent results and keeps instruction-like target text out of architecture.md and the ledger, which are pasted verbatim into later prompts.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: fix: reject duplicate object keys in findings.json
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
## What was wrong

`validate-findings.cjs` passes the file to `JSON.parse`, which keeps the **last** occurrence of a repeated object key. `enforceJsonTextLimits` scans the text before parsing, but it only counts nesting and array items, not object keys. So a record can say two different things, and the validator checks only the last one.

## Input that triggers it

```json
[{"verdict":"rejected","fingerprint":"a","title":"t","description":"d","claimed_root_cause":"c",
  "trace":[{"kind":"sink","file":"src/a.c","line":1,"scope":"s","description":"d"}],
  "evidence":[{"file":"src/a.c","line":1,"description":"d"}],
  "reason":"r","reason":"Second reason silently replaces the first."}]
```

On `main`: `PASS: 1 findings valid`. The same applies to `"verdict":"needs_validation","verdict":"rejected"`, or to a repeated `"line"` inside a trace entry.

## Fix

`enforceJsonTextLimits` now tracks whether each object expects a key next. It decodes every key with `JSON.parse` and keeps the decoded keys in a per-object `Set`. A repeated key fails with `input has duplicate object key "<key>"`, and the key is escaped with the existing `safeQuote`, so it can't inject control bytes into the output.

Keys are compared after decoding, the same way `JSON.parse` compares them:
- `"verd\u0069ct"` and `"verdict"` are treated as duplicates and rejected.
- `"a"` and `"A"` are different keys, so they're still accepted. So are `"\u00e9"` and `"e\u0301"`.
- The same key in different objects, such as two findings that both have `"verdict"`, is still accepted.

## Tests

```
node --test skills/security-audit/validate-findings.test.cjs
# tests 36, pass 36, fail 0
```

This adds two tests:
- `CLI rejects duplicate object keys instead of keeping the last one` fails on `main`.
- `CLI keeps distinct decoded keys and identical keys in separate objects` guards against rejecting valid input.

The coverage-ledger validator has the same hole, but in its own parser, so it's fixed in a separate PR.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: fix: allow artifact sharing within an attempt
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
## Summary
Fixes a bug in `validateAttempts()` where the validator incorrectly rejected artifact sharing between checks within the same attempt.

## Root Cause
Artifacts were added to `priorArtifacts` while the validator was still processing checks in the current attempt. This caused subsequent checks using the same artifact path to be incorrectly flagged as reusing evidence from an earlier attempt.

## Solution
- Added an `attemptArtifacts` set to collect artifacts for the current attempt.
- Checked artifacts against `priorArtifacts` to detect reuse from earlier attempts.
- Added the current attempt's artifacts to `priorArtifacts` only after all checks in that attempt have been validated.
- Preserved existing cross-attempt reuse checks and owner assignment validation.

## Tests
- Added a regression test to verify that checks within the same attempt can share an artifact.
- Added a test to ensure artifact reuse across different attempts is still rejected.
- Ran `node --test skills/security-audit/validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs`.
- Confirmed that the active tests pass with zero failures; seven tests are skipped.

cloudflare/security-audit-skill.title: fix: reject a coverage unit that excludes its own ordinary attack-class block
cloudflare/security-audit-skill.body:
## What was wrong

RECONNAISSANCE.md defines `excluded_blocks` as "every considered but unselected block and the source fact that excludes it". The validator already enforces this for companion blocks: a block that appears in both `selected_companion_blocks` and `excluded_blocks` fails with `block is also selected`. The ordinary block gets no such check. A unit can use a block as its `ordinary_attack_class_block` and exclude that same block as irrelevant, and the ledger passes.

## Input that triggers it

```json
"ordinary_attack_class_block": "ATTACK-CLASSES.md#Access control",
"excluded_blocks": [{"block": "ATTACK-CLASSES.md#Access control", "reason": "Claimed irrelevant."}]
```

On `main`, `validateDocument` returns no errors for this unit.

## Fix

When `ordinary_attack_class_block` is a string, every `excluded_blocks[].block` is compared with it. A match fails with `$[i].excluded_blocks[j].block: block is also the ordinary attack-class block`, which mirrors the existing selected/excluded check. When `ordinary_attack_class_block` is `null` (no ordinary block applies), the unit can still exclude that block.

## Tests

```
node --test skills/security-audit/validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
# tests 31, pass 31, fail 0
```

The extended `validates assignment block maps` test fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

Nutlope/hallmark.title: Name the theme in the app scaffold command
Nutlope/hallmark.body:
`flow.md` tells an app-screen build to run `theme.mjs scaffold --scope app`. That command has no theme slug. `scope` is not in `VALUED`, so `positional()` keeps the next token, and `app` becomes the slug.

`node theme.mjs scaffold --scope app` exits 1: `no theme at .../references/themes/app.md`.

The sentence above the command says the theme lends its palette, its faces, its radius and its surfaces. `usage()` already shows the working form, `scaffold <slug> [--scope app]`. The parenthetical now says `theme.mjs scaffold <slug> --scope app`.

Verified with `theme.mjs scaffold bloom --scope app`: it writes the stamp `shape: app screen` and the fixed app type scale (`--text-xs: 0.75rem`, no `clamp`). `node skills/hallmark/scripts/refcheck.mjs --errors` is clean across 99 reference files.

The gate list in that same sentence is unchanged.

Nutlope/hallmark.title: Read --scope as a flag instead of a slug
Nutlope/hallmark.body:
`theme.mjs` reads `--scope` with `flag()`, but `scope` is missing from `VALUED`, the set of flags whose next token is a value. `positional()` only skips that next token when the flag is in the set, so the value becomes a positional argument.

`node theme.mjs scaffold --scope app bloom` therefore looks up `references/themes/app.md` and exits 1 (`no theme at .../themes/app.md`). The same leak makes `photos "sea" --scope app` search for a second subject named `app`. `scaffold bloom --scope app` happens to work only because the slug comes first and later positionals are ignored.

`scope` is now in `VALUED`, beside `redesign`.

Verified with `theme.mjs`:
- `scaffold --scope app bloom` writes Bloom's tokens, the stamp `shape: app screen`, and the fixed app type scale (no `clamp`).
- `scaffold bloom --scope app` still does.
- `scaffold --scope app` with no slug prints usage and exits 2, instead of looking up a theme named `app`.
- `photos "sea" --n 1 --seed abc --scope app --json` returns the subject `sea` only.

The app-screens sentence in `flow.md` still shows `theme.mjs scaffold --scope app` with no slug. That command has nothing to scaffold; this change only stops `app` from being read as the theme.

Nutlope/hallmark.title: Run the mechanical width checks at 1440 too
Nutlope/hallmark.body:
`references/responsive.md` says the mechanical half runs at eight widths, including 1440: horizontal scroll and `overflow-x: clip` (34), wrapping controls (49), image tracks and display heads (50), radio tabs (53), stacked sticky elements (56). Gate 34 is "Horizontal scroll at any width 320 to 1920".

Those checks live in `observe()`, and `observe()` only runs on `WIDTHS`. That array was `[320, 375, 414, 768, 1024, 1280, 1920]`. The existing `1440×900` pass calls `observeSpace()`, which scores fold and space (F17, F18, 59, 69). It does not run the scroll or wrapping checks, so 1440 was a hole between 1280 and 1920.

`WIDTHS` is now `[320, 375, 414, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920]`, the same list `responsive.md` names. Fold, contrast, and the sticky check stay on the 1280 pass (`width === 1280`). Screenshots stay at 1280 and 375. README already says "eight widths", so it is unchanged.

Verified with a node check that the array matches the eight numbers in `responsive.md`, and that the `observe()` call sits on the `WIDTHS` loop while `observeSpace()` stays on the separate `1440×900` / `1920×1080` loop.

Nutlope/hallmark.title: fix: reject invalid hook settings before rewriting configuration
Nutlope/hallmark.body:
## Summary

labels.name: needs maintainer review
labels.description: Ready for a maintainer to review or decide

pbakaus/impeccable.body:
## Before opening

- Linked issue: #560


## Summary

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1), on maintainer instruction.

Since #559 the static engine skips the contrast check when a `url()` image backs text, so CLI scans, CI gates, and the hook never caught white copy on a near-white photo. Outside a browser there is no CORS and no canvas taint, so the engine now reads the image itself.

**How it works**

- A walk from the text up its ancestors stops at the first `url()` layer. If that layer is the ground, the engine decodes the image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP through the pure-Rust `image` crate the workspace already carries), scales it to at most 640px, and reads a 6x6 grid of pixels. Local files and base64 data URIs are read; remote URLs, missing or oversized files, and SVG keep today's skip.
- A static scan has no layout, so the verdict is coarse: the finding fires only when the 90th-percentile ratio fails. White text on a half-dark photo passes; white text on a light texture fails wherever it sits. Same `low-contrast` id, labeled snippet:

  ```
  sampled (coarse) 2.5:1 (need 4.5:1) — text #fdfdfd on light.png; p90 of 36 samples, median 2.4:1
  ```

- It stays silent where it cannot know. Uniform tints composite exactly; a gradient that varies, or has a stop the engine cannot read (`transparent`, a named color), is a scrim and keeps the skip. Each axis of the layer is filled, a known length, or unknown, and a layer with an unknown or sub-160px axis is decoration. Text hidden on purpose over its image is not measured: alpha at or below 0.1, a visually-hidden label, `font-size: 0`, or a `text-indent` that throws the line out of its box (`-9999px`, `100%`) on the text or an ancestor.
- Over an opaque fallback color (`background: #111 url(hero.jpg) center / cover`) the image is the ground only when it provably fills the box. Then its pixels replace the analytic check against that color; otherwise the analytic result stands as on main.
- The cascade carries what this needs beside the vector-pinned shorthand expansion, never inside it: `backgroundRepeat` / `backgroundSize`, the image reset for a color-only `background`, and a color named after the image.
- A stylesheet linked from another directory has its urls resolved against itself on the parsed value. The css text the pattern checks read is never rewritten.

**Departures from the issue's sketch:** 36 grid points rather than 9 (the overlay samples inside the text rect; here the grid must cover the image); no precise mode (the text position stays unknown even with container dimensions); no remote fetch (the hook runs on every edit); severity unchanged.

**Review rounds:** the Greptile and Cursor Bugbot rounds are in the follow-up commits. The maintainer's first review (false findings, correctness, hook-path performance) is addressed in 2687607f0 (with bot follow-ups through 74dd6b5c1) and walked item by item in [this comment](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/pull/806#issuecomment-5986772691). The second review (speed in the hook) is addressed in a5a6f089c: the edit hook never decodes an image, `detect` samples the page's images and writes a persistent cache the hook reads, no thumbnail, a truncated JPEG is undecodable; walked item by item in [this comment](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/pull/806#issuecomment-6236350860).

**Validation:** fixture `sampled-image-contrast.html` (+ `sampled-images/`) with twelve flag and nineteen pass cases; goldens recorded for the new cases and the directory sweeps re-recorded, noted in `tests/oracle/DELTAS.md`; an end-to-end test per review item in `crates/html/tests/sampled_contrast.rs` and unit tests for each decision; `cargo test --workspace` (one unrelated comp-verbs test fails on the dev machine, on main as well), `bun run test`, `bun run build`, and both wasm `cargo check` configurations pass. The tracked in-page bundle is regenerated with `cargo xtask bundle`; no rule was added, so its registry JSON is unchanged.

pbakaus/impeccable.body:
Fixes #1142.

## What was wrong

`resolve_length_px` (`crates/foundation/src/css/measures.rs`) knew px, rem, em and `%`. Every other suffix fell through to the unitless branch, `num * font_size_px`, so `15pt` was 15em. Print stylesheets set in points then drew false findings in the static engine (`impeccable detect <file>.html` and the Stop pass):

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| issue repro: `body{font-size:15px} h1{font-size:15pt}` | `oversized-h1`: `225px h1` | clean |
| `h1{font-size:30pt}` (40px) | `480px h1` | clean |
| `p{font-size:15px; line-height:0.3in}` (28.8px, 1.92x) | `tight-leading`: `0.30x` | clean |

Reproduced on main at 9368675 (engine 0.1.17) and on the installed 0.1.16 binary.

One correction to the report. The `tight-leading 0.15x` for `line-height: 1.5` does not reproduce on main with the minimal repro; only `oversized-h1` fires there. The `tight-leading` mechanism I could reproduce is a `line-height` in an absolute unit: `0.3in` over 15px was read as 0.3em (4.5px). A `pt` font size alone did not trigger it in any of my probes: read as ems it is far past the 24px display-type cutoff (`LEADING_DISPLAY_TYPE_PX`), which the rule skips.

## The fix

`absolute_length_px(value, num)` maps pt, pc, in, cm, mm and Q (any case) to px at 1in = 96px = 72pt = 6pc = 2.54cm = 25.4mm = 101.6Q, and `resolve_length_px` calls it before the unitless fall-through. The unit is the whole trailing run of ASCII letters, compared without allocating, so `vmin`, `cqmin` and friends are not taken for inches.

I left `resolve_font_size_px` in `quality.rs` alone. It has the same fall-through, but the cascade already rewrites every `font-size` to px through `resolve_length_px` (`cascade/values.rs`), so no input reaches its unit branch. I probed plain rules, inline style, `!important`, `@media`, `var()` and inherited `em` and `%` against a build with and without a change there, and the output was identical in every case; there is nothing to test, so I did not add it.

## Tests and fixtures

- `crates/html/tests/absolute_units.rs` (new): each unit at the same 96px through the whole static engine under `body{font-size:10px}` (so the em fall-through lands far from the truth in every unit, `pc` included), the same at 48px for the pass side, the issue repro, absolute-unit line-heights, and case-insensitivity. 7 tests, all red on main (checked).
- `cascade_units.rs`: all six units through `resolve_length_px` with a font-size context of 99, so a fall-through would show.
- `measures.rs`: `absolute_length_px` reads the whole unit (`vmin`, `cqmin`, `10px`, empty, non-ASCII tail all return `None`).
- `oversized-h1.html`: should-flag 60pt, 1.2in, 3cm; should-pass 30pt, 10mm, 40Q, 2.5pc. On main the pass rows read `480px`, `160px`, `640px` and the inch and centimetre flag rows fell under the threshold.
- `tight-leading.html`: should-flag 12pt over 15.5pt (1.29x) and 0.2in over 0.256in (1.28x); should-pass leading of 0.6cm, 0.25in and 16pt. On main the pass rows read `0.60x`, `0.25x`, the inch flag row read `0.26x` and the pt flag row was missed.
- The real-Chrome `crates/browser/tests/text_geometry.rs` flags exactly the two new tight-leading rows (1.29x, 1.28x) and none of the pass rows, so the URL engine agrees with the static engine; its expected count goes from 10 to 12.

## Hook cost

`cargo run --release -p impeccable-html --example rule_cost -- --runs 9 <inputs>` with 380 inputs: the 217 fixtures in `tests/fixtures/antipatterns` (identical copy for both sides) plus 163 `.html`/`.css`/`.tsx`/`.jsx` files of a real project. Main (9368675) and this branch, interleaved, cold, ms per edit. Two pairs on the final tree:

| | static-html mean | p50 | p95 | `quality-rules` mean | text engine mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, pair 1 | 22.86 | 21.95 | 32.42 | 0.368 | 5.71 |
| branch, pair 1 | 21.08 | 20.30 | 28.94 | 0.332 | 5.14 |
| main, pair 2 | 24.73 | 23.33 | 37.89 | 0.401 | 6.25 |
| branch, pair 2 | 21.99 | 21.37 | 30.65 | 0.349 | 5.75 |

No measurable cost. The branch is not faster; this machine drifts more between runs of the same binary (main alone ranged from 21.3 to 24.7 ms static-html mean across four rounds) than between main and branch. The new code runs only for a value that is not px, rem, em or `%`, and costs one scan over its trailing letters. An earlier pair on a slightly earlier revision (21.31 vs 21.30 and 22.72 vs 22.06 mean) agrees.

## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 2334 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored, exit 0 (Windows, rustc 1.98.1).
- The four per-fixture oracle goldens are re-recorded, each gaining exactly the new findings (three and two) and losing none; `oracle_html` (the static engine against those goldens) passes on the final tree.
- Not run: `bun run test`, the live and skill-behavior suites.

## Things you should know

- **Goldens were recorded on Windows.** The oracle's path masking is POSIX-only, so I replayed the corpus through a small local shim that maps Windows path spellings onto the committed tags. Before using it for the four cases, I checked it on the other 500 per-fixture goldens: all replay byte-equal. CI on Linux is the real check.
- **The in-page bundle is not refreshed.** `crates/live/assets/detect-antipatterns-browser.js` carries this code as wasm, and `docs/ENGINE.md` says to run `cargo xtask bundle` after touching `crates/foundation`. On pristine main on my machine that bundle does not rebuild byte-for-byte (`antipatterns.json` does), which `ci.yml` already says to expect across wasm-pack and wasm-opt versions, so I did not commit a 3 MB wasm blob built on a different toolchain. The registry is untouched, so the `antipatterns.json` gate is unaffected. Could you run `cargo xtask bundle` when you merge?
- **Sweeps not re-recorded.** `detect-dir-*`, `detect-scope-type`, `detect-scope-both` and `detect-no-advisory-*` also gain the five new findings, but they are accepted deltas the oracle does not compare, so I followed the earlier entries and left them. `DELTAS.md` has the entry.
- I did not bump `ENGINE_VERSION`.

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code).

## Before opening

This repo is issue-first for outside contributions. If you are not `pbakaus` or `abdulwahabone`, please link the issue where a maintainer approved or requested this PR. Unsolicited PRs may be closed without review.

- Linked issue: #950

  - [ ] I am `pbakaus` or `abdulwahabone`
  - [x] A maintainer approved this PR in the linked issue

## Summary

Fixes #950. Scope is limited to `inert` subtrees, as agreed in the issue. `aria-hidden` and `visibility: hidden` are left for a follow-up.

**Cause.** `text-occlusion` (victims), `nested-cards` and `cramped-padding` all pass through the shared paint walk in `crates/core/src/browser/painted.rs`. That walk consulted `inert` only in `closed_inert_dialog`, so an inert box counted as unpainted only when it was a dialog. Separately, `branch_z` returned no level for a branch with no positioned box, so `buried_by_an_opaque_sibling` skipped every level of an in-flow wrapper. The issue's `<div inert>` under `<main style="position:absolute; inset:0; z-index:40; background:#fff">` was therefore never seen as covered. Hit-testing skips inert content, so the occlusion probe at its text returned the overlay and reported it as 100% covered.

**Fix** (same file, same shape as #1102's dialog case):

- `closed_inert_dialog` becomes `buried_inert`. It takes `inert` on any box that an opaque positioned sibling, stacked above it, holds whole. The dialog requirement is dropped. "Inert alone" still does not count: an inert box that nothing opaque covers stays painted. That covers the page behind a modal over a translucent backdrop, an inert chat panel on screen, `#flag-inert-section` and `#flag-inert-dialog`.
- The stacking level is read from the reported element, not the inert root. A bar fixed above the cover inside an inert view therefore keeps its text. Containment still reads the root's box, as before.
- In `branch_z`, a branch with no positioned box now stacks at 0 in tree order. This is the conservative reading: a positioned `auto`/0 sibling earlier in tree order does not count as covering it. A numeric `z-index` on a box that is not positioned (a flex or grid item stacks by it) leaves the level unknown, so nothing is taken.
- One existing FakeDom twin changed. In `a_dialog_switched_off_with_inert_is_not_painted`, the "drawer open" step removed `inert` from the nav but left it on the inner panel, which still sits under the opaque sheet. The generalised check now reads that panel as buried, which is what the page would show. The step now strips `inert` from the panel too, which keeps its stated intent ("no `inert`, and its text is painted").

Cost: the `inert` attribute check comes first at every level of the walk. The sibling scan therefore runs only for an element under an inert root that already produced a gated finding.

Known limits, the same as the existing dialog path and noted in the doc comment: a cover's `clip-path`/mask and the top layer are not read, and only the cover's own sibling box is read, not its descendants.

- `crates/core/src/browser/painted.rs`: the fix, plus a FakeDom regression `an_inert_view_an_opaque_overlay_buries_is_not_painted` with its twins.

- `crates/browser/tests/inert_under_overlay.rs`: a real-Chrome test asserting each rule separately on both columns.

makecindy/cindy.title: bug(media): userData 经 junction/symlink 重定向后媒体全部无法入库（cindy-media: blob ancestor is a symlink），且完全静默

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

makecindy/cindy.body:
## 现象

把 Cindy 的数据目录（`app.getPath("userData")`）重定向到其他磁盘之后，**所有媒体写入静默失败**，用户侧看到的是：

- 创建伙伴失败，UI 只说「无法创建」，不给原因
- 往对话里发图片：图片在当轮能正常显示，但**不入库**；之后回看历史时图片丢失
- 更换伙伴头像失败

全程没有任何用户可见的提示，只有主进程日志里能看到：

```
local-db:bots:create
Error: cindy-media: blob ancestor is a symlink
  code: ELOOP
    at lstatRegularDir
    at prepareBlobDestination
    at writeBlob$1
    at storeTeammateAvatarImage
    at createBotProfile
```

```
image-cache:from-buffer
Error: cindy-media: blob ancestor is a symlink
    at ingestChatImageBuffer
[UseAttachments] cacheImageFromBuffer failed
```

## 环境

- Windows，Cindy 0.1.115
- `%APPDATA%\Cindy` 是 **Junction**，指向 `D:\CindyData\Cindy`

## 根因

两个点叠加：

1. `getBlobsRoot()` 把媒体根目录固定为 `path.join(app.getPath("userData"), "cindy-media", scope)`，不可配置。
2. `prepareBlobDestination()` 用 `lstatRegularDir` 逐级检查祖先目录，只要有任何一级是 reparse point 就直接抛 `ELOOP: cindy-media: blob ancestor is a symlink`。

而 C 盘空间紧张是很常见的情况，Windows 上把 userData 放到其他盘，唯一手段就是 symlink/junction。`XDT_USER_DATA_DIR` 经过验证只在 `!app.isPackaged` 时生效（`shouldSkipLegacyMigrationForDevSandbox`），正式版没有提供官方的数据目录迁移入口。

结果是一个死角：**越需要省 C 盘空间的用户，越容易踩到这个坑，而且完全无感。**

本机实测：10-03 把数据目录迁走之后，`cindy-media/blobs` 在之后 **50 天里新增 0 个文件**（最后一次写入是迁移前一天）。这期间一直在正常用 Cindy 发图、建过伙伴，没收到过任何报错。

## 复现

1. 完全退出 Cindy
2. 把 `%APPDATA%\Cindy` 换成 junction：`mklink /J "%APPDATA%\Cindy" "D:\CindyData\Cindy"`
3. 启动 Cindy，往对话里发一张图片
4. `cindy-media\blobs` 没有新增文件；主进程日志出现上面的 ELOOP

## 建议

1. **修根因**：在 `prepareBlobDestination` 里先对根路径做一次 realpath 归一化（`fs.realpath`），再逐级检查祖先。归一化之后 junction/symlink 就不再是「祖先」，但安全检查依然成立。
2. **补功能**：提供官方可用的数据目录迁移入口（现在这个能力只在开发态可用）。
3. **兜底**：blob 写入失败时给用户可见提示，不要只写日志。否则数据一直在悄悄丢，用户根本不会发现。

## 关于安全校验的说明

理解 `lstatRegularDir` 的初衷是防止目录穿越。归一化之后校验真实路径同样能达到这个目的：realpath 会把链接目标解出来，再判断落点是否仍在该在的根之内，攻击者依旧无法把写入引出授权范围。

makecindy/cindy.title: bug: 同一伙伴在另一台设备聊天后，本机伙伴被标记 demoted/shadowed 而消失，接管因 AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE 一直失败

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

makecindy/cindy.body:
### 问题描述 / What happened

同一个伙伴在不同电脑上聊天后，本机侧边栏里的伙伴会消失。我有两个伙伴「网络」「网络总管」，都因为跨设备使用而不见了。数据本身没有丢，只是本机入口被隐藏/降级。

### 环境 / Environment

- Cindy 0.1.112（macOS，Darwin 25.6.0）
- 同一账号三台设备：本机 MacBook Air（lujing）、另一台 MacBook Air（张庆伟的MacBook Air）、一台 Windows（DESKTOP-IXBIDTG）

### 复现步骤 / Steps to reproduce

1. 同一账号在多台电脑登录，其中一台（或手机来源）创建伙伴 A。
2. 在另一台电脑上打开/继续与伙伴 A 的对话（「网络」是在张庆伟的 MacBook Air 上创建并聊天；「网络总管」是 `bot_mobile_…` 来源，在 Windows 机上聊天）。
3. 回到本机：这两个伙伴不在伙伴列表里。

### 排查结果（脱敏）

- 本机云同步状态 `owners/<owner>/companion-cloud/<hash>.json` 中，两个伙伴都带 `demoted: true`；`companion-cloud/shadowed.json` 列出了这两个 id：`["bot_1792454737018_1zdv5o", "bot_mobile_005a…"]`。
- 「网络」`bot_1792454737018_1zdv5o`：本机 `bots/` 下没有目录、`bot_profiles` 表没有记录，也没有 `roomId`/`mirror`/`prefsSeeded`，本机只有设备镜像缓存里的会话摘要，因此本机完全没有它的入口。
- 「网络总管」`bot_mobile_005a…`：本机 `bot_profiles` 里仍是 `status=active`，`bots/` 下目录、记忆、工作区脚本都在；同时 `companion-cloud-backups/` 有接管前的备份。但被标记为 demoted/shadowed，路由日志每次都是 `routine skipped: teammate runs on another computer`。
- 日志（2026-10-19）：`Companion local copy backed up before take-over` → `Companion take-over could not finish locally { code: 'AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE' }` → `Companion take-over will retry { code: 'AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE' }`，接管一直没成功，也没有可退出的入口，之后 `demoted` 状态一直保留。

### 根因推测

1. 伙伴在别的设备上被使用后，云端把「主人电脑」判给了那台设备，本机副本被标记 `demoted` 并写入 `shadowed.json`，这个标记之后没有任何 UI 能清除。
2. 本机发起接管时，因为 `AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE`（头像资源拿不到）一直失败并重试，接管状态机被头像这种非关键资源卡死，demoted 状态无法恢复。
3. 对手机来源（`bot_mobile_…`）和后创建、本机从未同步过资料的伙伴（「网络」），本机没有任何兜底入口，用户看到的就是「伙伴消失」。

### 期望

- 伙伴被别的电脑使用后，本机至少保留一个「查看 / 在这台电脑接管」入口，而不是直接隐藏。
- 接管不应被头像等非关键资源（`AVATAR_UNAVAILABLE`）阻塞；失败应给出具体原因和可手动退出 demoted 的操作。
- 提供「恢复被隐藏的伙伴」入口，列出 `shadowed.json` 里的伙伴并可一键还原。

### 相关

与 #6204（换电脑执行后本机卡在准备中并丢失入口）、#6321（两台电脑共用云端身份，另一台的伙伴被隐藏且无法恢复）同类，但触发路径是「仅在另一台设备上聊天」，且包含手机来源伙伴和头像不可用导致的接管失败，供合并或参考。

makecindy/cindy.title: feat: 支持将 OpenCode 作为 Agent 引擎接入
makecindy/cindy.body:
### 使用场景 / Use case

OpenCode（anomalyco/opencode，MIT，19.2 万 star）是当前社区使用最广的开源编码 agent，许多开发者已把它作为日常主力工具。目前 Cindy 已支持 Codex / Claude Code（PR #1265 在推进 Pi agent），但还不支持 OpenCode。希望能在 Cindy 中像选其他 agent 一样直接创建 OpenCode 会话，复用统一的会话树、用量、权限审查与远程协同能力。

### 当前问题 / Current limitation

- Agent 运行时 VendorKey 只支持 claude 和 codex（agent-binaries/types.ts:13），无法注册 OpenCode。
- 当前仅有模型供应商层面的 OpenCode Go 预设（#527），不能创建 OpenCode 会话、管理授权或统计用量。
- 无法将 OpenCode 会话接入 Orca 协同、定时任务与多端同步。

### 期望方案 / Proposed solution

参照现有 Claude Code / Codex 的 vendor 模式（可参考 #1265 对 Pi 的接入方式）分阶段推进：
1. 核心接入：OpenCode CLI/SDK 桥接与 translator、二进制分发、会话创建/resume、基础模型路由；
2. 授权与用量：BYOM provider、用量/缓存统计、额度展示；
3. 协同与多端：Orca worker、定时任务、device-link/mobile 适配。

作为新增 agent，不影响既有行为；OpenCode 二进制缺失时跳过注册。

### 已考虑的替代方案 / Alternatives considered

1. 仅通过 OpenCode Go 模型预设使用：只能覆盖模型层，无 agent 级会话与用量能力；
2. 自定义 provider + API Key：同样是模型层，拿不到会话树/fork/resume 等能力；
3. 自行在终端操作 OpenCode：偏离 Cindy 统一管理 agent 的定位。

makecindy/cindy.body:
## 这次改了什么

### 摘要

伙伴私聊引用长消息时，摘要在 279 个 UTF-16 单元处截断。如果这里恰好位于 emoji 的代理对之间，会保留一个孤立高代理项，显示成乱码。例如 `'a'.repeat(278) + '😀x'` 原来得到 `278 个 a + \ud83d + …`。

仅在截断边界跨过完整代理对时将边界前移一位，输出变为 `278 个 a + …`。保留现有 280 UTF-16 单元上限、空白折叠、省略号以及未超限文本的行为。Desktop 和 Mobile 均复用此共享函数。

### 变更类型

debpalash/VoiceStudio.title: ui(workflows): workflow list, template picker, canvas step palette and inspector
debpalash/VoiceStudio.body:
Cleans up the Workflows page (`/workflows`) based on the owner's screenshot review.

**Layout**
- The left pane now lists only your workflows (with **New**) and a **New from template** entry. That entry opens a picker with icons and short descriptions, grouped into Narration, Audio and Calls. The old Templates and Add a step lists are gone from the rail.
- The step palette is now a compact floating toolbar on the canvas edge. Click adds a step, wired to the selected step when that step has a free output (conditions fill yes, then no). You can also drag a step onto the canvas. Each button has a tooltip, it is reachable with Tab, and the arrow, Home and End keys move between buttons.
- The workflow name is an inline-editable title in the header, with a subtle **Saved** indicator and Run / Duplicate / Delete beside it. The jargon subtitle is replaced by a single plain line.

**Steps**
- Nodes show a short summary that wraps instead of being cut off. A step missing a required setting (scripts, audio clips, voice, languages or condition phrase) shows a **Needs setup** badge instead. This mirrors the per-step checks in `compileWorkflow` (`stepSetupIssue`).
- **Run workflow** is disabled while any step needs setup. The note beside it ("Speak needs setup") gives the reason and opens that step.
- The inspector gets a header with the step icon, a close button (Esc also closes it) and a setup notice. Selecting a step with Enter or Space on the canvas opens the inspector and moves focus into it.

**Canvas chrome**
- The minimap is smaller and faded until hovered.
- The React Flow attribution is kept, because hiding it is meant for Pro subscribers, but it is faded until hovered.

**Other**
- The page is split into focused components, all under 500 lines: `use-workflow-library`, `workflow-title-bar`, `workflow-step-palette`, `workflow-step-node`, `workflow-inspector`, `workflow-template-picker`, `workflow-delete-dialog`.
- 23 new strings, translated into all 21 locales.
- Docs updated: `docs/electron-workflows.md` and `docs/calls.md`.
- No backend changes. The Workflows / Calls switch is unchanged.

**Tests**
- New `workflow-setup.test.ts`: checks that setup issues match the `compileWorkflow` rejections, and covers adding a step after a selected one, including wiring and condition branches.
- Workflow canvas and execution smokes updated for the template picker, the palette and the title field. They now also check the Needs setup badges, the disabled Run and its reason link, and arrow-key movement in the palette.
- Ran locally: vitest for `features/workflows` (61 passed), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run locale:check`, `vp lint`, and the renderer smokes `workflow-canvas-smoke` and `workflow-execution-smoke` (both pass).

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

## Summary

Restore complete opt-in native Windows ROCm provisioning in this PR for both Electron and source setup, using a single Windows-specific recipe rather than Linux-only wheels.

Refs #2468: this addresses Windows provisioning and compatible main-runtime routing; the broader hardware/engine parity issue remains open. Overlap is documented with #2600, #2607 and #2908; their hardware evidence is separate from this PR's validation.

## Changes

- Explicit Windows x64 `OMNIVOICE_TORCH_VARIANT=rocm` selects Python 3.12, AMD's pinned ROCm 7.2.1 Torch/audio/vision stack and SDK components, and the official HIP CTranslate2 4.8.2 wheel.
- Verify the CT2 archive/member SHA-256 and installed HIP library identity. Exclude locked Torch/CT2/CUDA packages before sync; keep the overlay during repair. Shared installation and verification serve both source and Electron.
- Reject incompatible interpreters, package versions, native imports, unavailable GPUs, failed synchronized GPU arithmetic and failed/timed-out native probes. Recipe/ABI changes invalidate readiness. Model-free readiness does not claim speech inference.
- Initialize local HIP DLL lookup for actual backend/probe processes; preserve CPU choices and existing CUDA/Linux/macOS behavior. Optional engines retain their version boundaries and explicit compatibility checks.
- Retain independent sentencepiece repair and bound Windows native application-import probes with actual child-process cleanup. Failed probes preserve the installing marker and user data for retry.
- Repair the ROCm overlay only after confirmed package/version/binary damage; GPU/driver/timeouts, malformed diagnostics and ambiguous external native failures stop without reinstalling. Import failures check recorded native files in the importing wheel and the explicitly pinned AMD SDK components.
- Reuse native verification only within a single read-only startup decision; independent checks and post-repair verification stay fresh.
- Include the recipe/helpers in desktop resources; preserve models/projects through setup retries. Add an optional offline CT2 speech smoke requiring explicit local model/WAV inputs.
- Update Windows guidance, README, all 21 loaded locale catalogs and the credited changelog. Merge current main before validation.

## Type

- [x] New feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Tests
- [x] Documentation

## Testing

- Current-main refresh (2026-10-23): merged main `87e142f4`, resolved all conflicts and retained one commit. 381 focused Windows ROCm/setup/compatibility tests pass with 1 platform skip; 88 Electron runtime tests and 589 locale/changelog/version checks pass. Both Node and web TypeScript checks pass. These targeted cohorts overlap earlier results; full upstream CI still requires maintainer approval.

- Final integrated offline ROCm/device/GPU-report/routing/source-setup cohort: 370 passed, 1 existing platform skip; one existing audioop deprecation warning. This includes the corrected legacy IndexTTS fixture and the new default/opt-in matrix. Source orchestration: 5 Node tests pass. Results below overlap this cohort.
- Offline provisioning/ASR/GPU/sidecar/performance coverage: 463 passed, 2 skipped. Latest repair/verification/integrity matrix: 145 passed, including real import-time SyntaxError/ValueError/AttributeError/TypeError cases, cancellation controls, damaged SDK and intact external-prerequisite cases; the earlier wider follow-up cohort passed 105. These cohorts overlap.

- Latest source prerequisite/guard follow-up: 18 Python and 5 Node tests pass; the missing-VC++ cases failed before the fix. Windows ROCm setup stops with manual installation guidance before any prerequisite download or installer process. Default setup behavior is preserved.
- Latest IndexTTS opt-in/default routing follow-up: 105 Python tests pass, with a separate 72-test focused rerun. Eight default-Windows routing cases failed before the fix. Unknown sidecar metadata is conservative only in explicit Windows ROCm mode; default behavior, known HIP/non-HIP handling and CPU choices remain intact across Windows/Linux/macOS. These cohorts overlap earlier results.
- Locale parity/changelog/version/CJK gates: 590 passed; all 21 Electron locale catalogs pass. Mobile contract: 4 passed, 1 skipped.

New modules/tests and scoped lint/format/diff/size checks pass. Legacy `scripts/setup.py` retains the same eight baseline Ruff diagnostics; none were introduced by the prerequisite fix.

Exact CT2 archive/member hashes were independently verified and the seven official AMD artifact URLs were checked.

Source setup checks the Visual C++ prerequisite locally; both source and installed Electron users must install/verify it manually as documented. Opted-in Windows ROCm setup does not automatically download this prerequisite.

debpalash/VoiceStudio.title: fix(omnivoice): free reference ASR before synthesis, encode references once, keep diagnostics private
debpalash/VoiceStudio.body:
Replaces #2619 by @alvig060121-afk, cherry-picked onto current main with their authorship kept.

## What it does (from #2619)
- Frees an implicitly loaded reference speech model before synthesis, so cloning on 8 GB unified-memory Macs no longer swaps until the recv deadline.
- Encodes a transcript-free reference once per sidecar (cached prompt path), instead of reloading ASR on every line.
- Trims the selected reference passage to pauses and re-transcribes it, keeping the untrimmed passage when the trim has no words or its transcription fails.
- Serializes reference-ASR load/use/release per model; releases recognizers that find no words before the next one loads; tries the resident winner first on later windows.
- Diagnostics are opt-in (`OMNIVOICE_DIAG=1`), memory numbers only, never the reference transcript.

## Maintainer fixes on top
- **No repeated unsuccessful ASR in one pass** (fixes the two failing `test_sidecar_preserves_supplied_text_and_local_fallback[*-False]` cases and CodeRabbit's "avoid repeating unsuccessful ASR before a prompt-cache hit"): the sidecar passes the outcome of its reference transcription (`empty` / `failed`) through `generate_with_cached_ref` to `_get_clone_prompt`, which skips the repeat. Only a completed empty attempt marks a cached prompt as trusted for the current recognizers; an error stays retryable. The encode-once sidecar tests now assert one ASR attempt per request (they had encoded the double call).
- **Per-model lock** is a module function `_reference_asr_lock(model)` storing the lock in the instance dict, so an instance attribute can never shadow it (see #3183 below).

## Bot findings
All earlier CodeRabbit/Greptile findings were checked against the current code: the snapshot-fixture finding (tests now use `_asr_snapshot`, which passes `_has_asr_weights`, and assert the loader ran), long-reference release, stale prompt after a recognizer change, ASR errors becoming cache hits, overlapping clones, long-reference trimming, overlapping fallback models, failed-recognizer release, winner-first ordering and winner reload are all addressed by the cherry-picked commits; the repeated-ASR finding is fixed here.

## Overlap with #3183 (open, @nirmalchatur)
A trial merge of #3183 onto this branch conflicts in `omnivoice/models/omnivoice.py` and `backend/services/asr_backend.py`; with the resolution below, both PRs' tests pass (228 passed). When #3183 lands, take care to:
1. **Use one lock.** #3183 adds its own `_reference_asr_lock(model)` (key `_reference_asr_lock`) plus `@_with_reference_asr`. This branch now uses the same name and key, so keep a single definition (this one has a creation guard). Do not reintroduce a *method* named `_reference_asr_lock`: #3183's instance-dict key would shadow it and raise `'RLock' object is not callable`.
2. **Keep both method blocks.** `_release_implicit_asr` (here) and `_reference_transcript` / `unload_asr_model` (#3183) go side by side.
3. **Re-read the trimmed passage with the selected engine.** Call `self._reference_transcript(...)` first, then fall back to `self.transcribe` only if `ensure_bundled_reference_asr()` succeeds, rather than always calling the bundled Whisper.
4. **`asr_backend.py`:** keep #3183's `_reference_transcriber_call` / `install_reference_transcriber` / `remove_reference_transcriber`, plus this branch's `_discover_reference_candidates` and `transcribe_reference`. Keep only one `transcribe_reference`.

JetBrains/thinkrail.title: fix(web): let an active IME own Enter, Escape and arrows in every text field
JetBrains/thinkrail.body:
## Problem

#384 stopped IME composition (Chinese Pinyin, Japanese, Korean) from sending early in the chat composer, but every other text field still acted on keys the IME owned. The Enter that should commit a candidate added a TODO step, a Plan task, or a rename with raw text such as `nihao` or a half-built Hangul syllable. The Escape that should cancel a composition also cancelled the rename or closed the field, losing what was typed. In the Ask card's Other field, ↑/↓ moved questionnaire focus instead of the IME candidate. Dialogs and popovers (sign-in prompt, Create workspace, model and branch pickers, …) closed on a composing Escape too, because Radix's document-level Escape listener does not check composition.

## Approach

- **One rule, applied everywhere:** while an IME owns the key (`isComposing`, or the legacy `keyCode` 229 sentinel for the final keydown after `compositionend`), Enter, Escape, arrows, Tab and shortcuts belong to the IME. Only a later ordinary key triggers the field's own behavior. This extends the existing `Composer` rule to every text field.
- **The guard lives in `@thinkrail/ui/keyboard`** (`isImeComposing`) because the app, `resource-renderers` and the ui primitives all need it. It replaces `prompt`'s `isPromptKeyEventComposing`. The app's `lib` was rejected as the home because neither `resource-renderers` nor `ui` can import it.
- **Dialogs and popovers are fixed once, in the primitives.** `DialogContent`, `DialogPanel` and `PopoverContent` wrap the caller's `onEscapeKeyDown` in `yieldEscapeToIme`, which `preventDefault`s a composing Escape so Radix keeps the layer open, without changing any call site. Menus hold no text fields and are left alone.
- **Drift guard:** the bug came from the rule being stated for `Composer` only. A source-scan unit test now fails when a file with a text field and a key handler doesn't use the guard. Allow-list entries carry their reason; the only one is `ProjectTree`, whose inputs use `workspaceActions`' guarded props.
- **Deliberately out of scope:** global modifier shortcuts (`Mod+K`, `Ctrl+R`, `Mod+W`) are app chords, not text-field keys, and stay ungated. `TerminalInstance`'s own 229 check translates xterm chords, which is a different rule, and stays as is.

## Changes

- **Text fields:** each field returns early on `isImeComposing` before handling any key.
  - The fields listed in #875: TODO add field, Plan add-task, History search (its input and its window-level Escape listener), chat-tab rename, closed-chat rename, layout preset name/rename, workspace/project rename, the extension text prompt, and the provider sign-in prompt.
  - Fields found during the audit: model context window, subagent settings, chat/file line width, JetBrains AI refresh interval, and the Review comment composer and comment editor (`resource-renderers`).
  - Handlers that already `stopPropagation` still do so first, so tab-strip and review keys stay contained.
- **Ask card:** the card's Shift+Escape skip and the note editor now use the full guard, which adds the 229 sentinel. The Other field yields before its ↑/↓/Enter handling.
- **New `@thinkrail/ui/keyboard` subpath:** `isImeComposing` and `yieldEscapeToIme`. The dialog and popover primitives use it, and `isPromptKeyEventComposing` is removed from `prompt`.
- **Tests:** `e2e/composer-ime.spec.ts` is renamed to `e2e/ime-composition.spec.ts` and shares one key dispatcher across the composer, the TODO add field (Enter), chat-tab rename (Escape/Enter), and the Create workspace dialog (Escape).
- **Specs:**
  - `apps/web/SPEC.md` states the app-wide rule, with the #875 post-mortem.
  - `packages/ui/SPEC.md` documents the guard, the 229 rationale, the primitives and the scan.
  - `chat/SPEC.md` and `chat/tools/SPEC.md` now link to the app-wide rule instead of restating it.

## Screenshots

Not applicable — no visual change. The fix changes keyboard handling only while an IME is composing; `e2e/ime-composition.spec.ts` is the before/after evidence (with the fix reverse-applied, its TODO, rename and dialog tests fail).

## Related issues

Closes #875

JetBrains/thinkrail.title: Support an Electrobun native channel alongside WebSocket for host traffic
JetBrains/thinkrail.body:
## Problem

The web client reaches the host only over one WebSocket. That suits the browser, CLI and remote use, but on desktop it means a loopback port, a reconnect path for a local call, and no fallback when the socket cannot bind (e.g. the Windows port collision already worked around in the launcher).

## Proposal

Let one host accept several kinds of connection at once: a trusted connection over the desktop shell's native channel, plus N authenticated WebSocket clients, all on the same host state.

- Keep `packages/contracts` transport-neutral and add a second transport behind the web client's transport interface, chosen by an injected parameter. `apps/web` stays independently shippable; browser and CLI keep the WebSocket.
- Add a host connection registry: per-connection identity, event fan-out, and auth (local channel trusted by construction, sockets use tokens).

## Why: security and stability

Ping improvement is not an expected; these are.

- Security: a native webview channel has no listening port, so no other local process or web page can reach the host through it. Today's loopback socket has to authenticate every connection instead. Encryption alone adds little on loopback and does not protect against script running inside the page, so the gain is the missing port, not the crypto.
- Stability: the desktop shell's own RPC already degrades between channels (socket, then the native webview bridge), while the host WebSocket has no alternative. Riding the shell's channel would inherit that resilience. Silent per-message fallback can hide a broken socket, so any switch should be observable.
- Remote access: the desktop app could also let other devices connect to its running host over WebSocket, while its own window keeps using the local channel. The window needs no token or port, and remote devices are the only ones that authenticate.

## Measuring

The webview and host are separate processes, so any local channel still crosses a process boundary, and some webview RPC layers use a loopback socket themselves. The AI provider’s response time matters much more than the overhead of sending tokens over a socket. Benchmark the current WebSocket on desktop before building anything:

- small-call round-trip latency
- 1–10 MB file read or diff throughput
- terminal-output flood
- cold-start connect and reconnect time

If the numbers are fine, the decision rests on the architecture and stability benefits above, weighed against a second transport and a larger test matrix.

## Alternatives

- Keep the WebSocket only.

## Problem

Skill and tool text that ThinkRail ships into every user's project points at ThinkRail's own source code:

- `choosing-a-workflow` names its location `packages/pi-thinkrail-workflow`;

## Problem

Currently, the application lacks internationalization (i18n) support and custom font configuration.

- **Limited font customization:** Users cannot choose their preferred fonts, which may affect readability and the overall user experience, especially for CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) languages.

- Support system-installed fonts and custom font files.
- Provide font configuration options in the application settings.
- Ideally, allow separate font settings for the UI and code/terminal areas, if applicable.

## Alternatives considered

- **Browser or system-level translation:** This may provide partial localization but often results in inconsistent translations and UI issues.
- **System-wide font configuration:** Changing system fonts affects other applications and doesn't provide application-specific flexibility.
- **Manually modifying styles or source code:** Possible for developers, but inconvenient and difficult to maintain across updates.

Native support for these features would provide a much better user experience.

## Additional context

These improvements would make the application more accessible and customizable for users worldwide, particularly those using CJK languages.

AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.title: fix(fetch): ignore charset= hidden in another meta attribute
AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.body:
## Summary

`decode_body` treated the first `charset=` inside any meta tag as the page encoding. An `og:image` URL such as `?charset=iso-8859-1` therefore overrode a later `<meta charset="utf-8">`, and a canonical `https://example.com/café` was decoded as `https://example.com/cafÃ©`. The sniffer now follows HTML's prescan: a `charset` attribute, or a `content` attribute only when `http-equiv` is `content-type`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature / sub-skill
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor / code quality
- [ ] Other (describe below)

## Problem

HTML's encoding prescan honors an attribute whose name is `charset`, or a `content` attribute when the same tag's `http-equiv` is `content-type` ([prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#prescan-a-byte-stream-to-determine-its-encoding)). The old regular expression matched `charset=` anywhere before the tag's `>`. A query string in `og:image` won, so later audit steps used the mojibake canonical. The same miss decoded a real `windows-1252` page as UTF-8 when an earlier image URL contained `charset=utf-8`.

## Change

`_extract_meta_charset` reads meta attributes. A `charset` attribute is the encoding. A `content` value is used only together with `http-equiv="content-type"`. `charset=` inside another attribute is ignored, so the later real `charset` attribute still wins. The Content-Type header is unchanged and still takes priority over the meta tag.

## Test results

```

canonical was https://example.com/cafÃ©
windows-1252 smart quote was replaced because the og:image query selected utf-8
```

```

12 passed
ruff check scripts/url_safety.py tests/test_fetch_page_decoding.py

AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.title: fix(sitemap): keep Sitemap URLs when a comment follows
AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.body:
## Summary

A `Sitemap:` line whose URL is followed by a `#` comment was ignored, so discovery never fetched that URL and only tried the four common paths. The same drop happened when a UTF-8 BOM sat in front of a `Sitemap:` line that was the first line of the file.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature / sub-skill
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor / code quality
- [ ] Other (describe below)

## Problem

Google's robots.txt syntax is `<field>:<value><#optional-comment>`: everything after `#` is a comment, and `sitemap` is one of the four fields ([robots.txt spec](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/robots-txt/robots-txt-spec)). RFC 9309 defines the same trailing comment (`EOL = *WS [comment] NL`) and says parsers may add a Sitemap line.

`_SITEMAP_LINE` required the URL to be the last token on the line, so `Sitemap: https://example.com/products.xml # primary catalog` produced no URL. Discovery then fetched `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/sitemap_index.xml`, `/sitemap-index.xml`, and `/wp-sitemap.xml`, and never `products.xml`. A file saved with a UTF-8 BOM failed the same way when `Sitemap` was the first line, because U+FEFF is not whitespace.

A line that is itself a comment (`# Sitemap: https://example.com/secret.xml`) stays ignored.

## Change

Strip a single leading U+FEFF, cut each line at the first `#`, then apply the existing Sitemap matcher. The URL that remains is the one that gets fetched.

## Test results

Before the fix, on `origin/main`:

```
python3 -m pytest tests/test_sitemap_discovery.py::test_sitemap_directive_keeps_its_url_when_a_comment_follows tests/test_sitemap_discovery.py::test_sitemap_directive_on_the_first_line_survives_a_utf8_bom tests/test_sitemap_discovery.py::test_commented_sitemap_directive_is_the_url_that_gets_fetched -q --tb=line
3 failed
commented directive parsed as []
BOM directive parsed as []
fetched URLs were only robots.txt and the four common paths; products.xml was absent
```

After the fix:

```

16 passed
```

`ruff check` reports a pre-existing import-sort finding on line 25 of `scripts/sitemap_discovery.py`. That line is unchanged from `origin/main`.

Graphify-Labs/graphify.title: fix(extract): report AST cache hit rate over the file total, not uncached set (#4740)

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

Graphify-Labs/graphify.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #4740. `graphify update` reported its AST cache progress against the uncached set, so the last line always read `N/N uncached files (100%)` and looked like a 100% hit rate. #4740 read it as "the copied cache missed almost every file"; the real rate was never printed anywhere.

That line counts progress through the work the run has to do, so its denominator is the work, not the corpus. This adds a separate line whose denominator is the file total, and leaves the existing progress lines alone.

**Before** (warm run across 100 `.py` + 20 `.ts`, cache already warmed, v8 `92741d16`):

```text
  AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

20 of the 120 files were re-extracted, and the only line shown says 100%.

**After:**

```text
cold:  AST cache: 0/120 files served from cache (0%); 120 to extract
warm:  AST cache: 100/120 files served from cache (83%); 20 to extract
       AST extraction: 20/20 uncached files (100%) [12 workers]
```

```diff
 graphify/extract.py
+  _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    hoisted to module scope, shared by all three sites
   extract()
+    cache_hits / no_extractor counters in the Phase 1 cache loop
+    print(f"  AST cache: {cache_hits}/{total} files served from cache "
+          f"({cache_hits * 100 // total}%); {len(uncached_work)} to extract"
+          + f"; {no_extractor} without an extractor")
+    gated on total >= _PROGRESS_INTERVAL, like the progress lines
   _extract_parallel / _extract_sequential
-    _PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 100    dropped, both read the module constant now
 tests/test_extract.py
+  test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total
```

No existing test changes. `tests/test_extract.py:5660` pins the `100/100 uncached files (100%)` format and still passes unmodified.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] Tests or CI
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Security fix

## Verification & Invariants

The cache summary reports against the files the run was asked to extract, so its denominator cannot shrink to the uncached set. The progress lines keep counting the uncached work, and their format stays pinned by `tests/test_extract.py:5660`.

- [x] **Read** the [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.
- [x] **Reproduced** the issue and identified the invariant.
- [x] Made the **smallest fix** necessary.
- [x] Added a **regression test** (if bug fix) or isolated boundary test.
- [x] Kept the PR description **synchronized** with the final implementation.
- [x] Documented any **limitations / unsupported cases** explicitly.

**Merge Danger**

**Door:** two-way. Two counters, one `print`, one test. No schema, cache or file-format change, no persisted state, nothing to migrate back.

**Blast Radius:** narrow, and limited to stdout:
- The line prints on the runs that already print progress, meaning any `extract()` call asked to extract `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files or more. Small batches, which is what `watch`, the hooks and the MCP server pass on a rebuild, stay quiet. Anything parsing that stdout strictly will see one extra line on the large runs. The gate came out of review: the first version printed on every call, so a one-file watch rebuild logged a 0% rate that is trivially true and carries no information.
- The counts come from the existing Phase 1 loop. Extraction, caching and the graph are untouched.
- Files with no extractor were invisible in every printed total before this. They now show as a suffix, so the 5 `.ets` files in the existing 105-file test are accounted for instead of silently absent.

**Limitations**

- The `uncached files` lines are unchanged. A reader still sees `20/20 uncached files (100%)`; the new line is what supplies the correct denominator. I left them because their format is asserted by an existing test, and rewriting them is outside this fix.
- On a TS-heavy repo the rate will read low or zero, because the JS/TS suffixes bypass the AST cache (`_JS_CACHE_BYPASS_SUFFIXES`). That is the second half of #4740 and this PR does not touch it.
- The `; N without an extractor` suffix is not asserted by a test. The path is exercised, since the existing 105-file test's `.ets` files have no extractor, but nothing pins the suffix text.
- Nothing prints when the path list is empty, or when it holds fewer than `_PROGRESS_INTERVAL` (100) files.
- Once warm `update` runs pass only the changed batch (the incremental path in #4740's other half), this line goes quiet on the runs someone might use to check whether the cache helped. If that visibility is wanted, it belongs behind a flag or an environment variable rather than unconditional stdout.

## How was this tested?

New `tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total` drives the real `extract()` over 100 `.py` + 5 `.ts` and reads captured stdout, no mocking. The corpus is sized past 100 files on purpose: the final progress line only prints when `total_files >= 100` (`extract.py:9263`), so a smaller corpus cannot show the two lines side by side. It covers three runs:

- cold, cacheable-only corpus -> `0/100`, `100 to extract`
- warm, same corpus -> `100/100`, `0 to extract`
- mixed, after warming -> `100/105`, `5 to extract`, while asserting the progress line still reads `5/5 uncached files (100%)` and that `105/105 uncached files` never appears

The gate was measured directly, in a scratch checkout, against the real `extract()` and through `_rebuild_code(changed_paths=[one file])`:

```text
    1 file  -> no line

  100 files -> prints
  605 files -> prints
one-file watch rebuild -> no line, only the usual watch message

tests/test_extract.py with the gate     -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
tests/test_extract.py without the gate  -> 373 passed, 1 xfailed
```

  tests/test_extract.py::test_extract_reports_ast_cache_hit_rate_over_file_total \

  -> 2 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
  -> 8727 passed, 15 skipped, 1 xfailed, 2225 warnings in 402.12s (0:06:42)

Environment note, not fixed here: the full suite needs `tests/test_skillgen_input_path_injection.py` to install `graphifyy` through `uv`, so it hangs without network. The step-1 script tries `uv tool run` / `uv tool install` before it ever reads the `graphify` shebang. With `graphify` on PATH and an offline `uv` that fails fast, that file's 30 tests pass in 8s.

Graphify-Labs/graphify.body:
Fixes #1769.

## What this fixes

`graphify-out/cost.json` is meant to be a running log of how many tokens each build used. Only the skill ever wrote to it. `graphify extract` printed the tokens for the run and then just dropped them, so if you refresh your graph with `extract` (on a schedule, say) the log stays stuck on the first build and you can't tell what refreshes cost you.

## What changed

- `graphify extract` now adds each run to `cost.json` the same way the skill does: date, input and output tokens, file count, plus the running totals
- works with and without `--no-cluster`, and honours `--out`
- an existing log from the skill is kept and added to
- a run that used no tokens (code only, nothing sent to a model) doesn't touch it
- if `cost.json` is broken and can't be read, it's left alone with a warning instead of being replaced with a fresh one-run log

## How I tested it

- ran it for real with Ollama (qwen2.5-coder:7b) on a small folder, changed a doc, ran it again. Before: `cost.json` never got written by `extract`. After: both runs are in it and the totals add up
- added `tests/test_extract_cost_ledger.py`. The three that check runs get added fail on current `v8` and pass with this change, the other two check a broken log and a no-token run are left alone
- full test suite: 8,422 passed. The 8 that fail (7 in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`) fail the same way on `v8` without this change

## Not in this one

- a run that gets stopped by the shrink guard still spent tokens but isn't logged, since it exits before the tokens are printed. Happy to add that if you want it counted
- the issue also mentions `cluster-only` and labelling, I kept this one to `extract`

Graphify-Labs/graphify.body:
## What does this PR do?

`_resolve_python_member_calls` folds labels across the whole corpus, so in a mixed corpus it binds member calls across languages:

- a Swift `Inner.go()` binds a Python class `Inner`;
- a Python `Inner.go()` binds a Swift `Inner`;
- a Python `SwiftArray.make()` binds a Swift node labelled `Swift.Array`, because the label key drops the dot;
- a Swift class with the same name as a Python class counts as a second definition in the single-definition guard, so a correct Python-to-Python member call binds nothing.

The fix: the pass skips callers and targets whose effective suffix (`.graphifyrc` language overrides honoured) belongs to another extractor, and counts only Python classes for the single-definition guard. Extensionless files (shebang scripts), unknown suffixes and raw calls that name no file still pass, as before. Other languages bind their member calls in their own passes.

Found during the Swift cross-file work (#4754), but independent of it: this PR does not depend on the Swift PR, and the Swift PR does not depend on this one.

Graphify-Labs/graphify.title: fix(js): keep nested functions scoped so same-named calls don't bind to them

labels.name: contributor
labels.description: Pull request from a returning community contributor

Graphify-Labs/graphify.body:
## What this fixes

Since #2653, a JS/TS function declared inside another function gets its own node, which is great. But it also went into the file-wide name lookup, so a call to that name from anywhere in the file could get linked to it, even from outside the function it lives in. Two ways this goes wrong:

- two functions that each have their own inner `run`: both get linked to the last one
- a function with an inner `helper` steals the callers of a top-level or imported `helper`

So the graph says things call functions they can't even see.

## How to recreate

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > x.ts <<'EOF'
export function helper() { return 0; }
export function a() { function helper() { return 1; } return helper(); }
export function b() { return helper(); }
EOF
graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster
python -c "import json; g=json.load(open('graphify-out/graph.json')); [print(e['source'], e['relation'], e['target']) for e in g['edges'] if e['relation'] == 'calls']"
```

Before:

```
x_a calls x_a_helper
x_b calls x_a_helper
```

`b()` is linked to the `helper` hidden inside `a()`. After:

```
x_a calls x_a_helper
x_b calls x_helper
```

Same thing with two inner functions of the same name:

```ts
export function first() { function run() { return 1; } return run(); }
export function second() { function run() { return 2; } return run(); }
```

Before, `first()` calls `x_second_run`. After, each calls its own.

## What changed

Python already handles this the right way (#3405), so I reused the same approach for JS/TS:

- each inner function is recorded under the function it's declared in
- a call (or a function passed by name, like `register(run)`) looks in its own scope first, then the outer ones
- inner functions are kept out of the file-wide lookup, since they can't be called from outside anyway

Top-level functions, imports and methods are looked up the same as before.

## How I tested it

- added `tests/test_js_nested_function_scope.py` with the cases above, an inner function named like an import, siblings and deeper nesting, and inner functions inside arrow components. The four that check the wrong links fail on current `v8` and pass with this change, the siblings one checks those still resolve
- ran it on five of my own JS/TS projects before and after. Four didn't change at all. The fifth has a minified Prisma runtime full of one-letter names, where calls that pointed into other functions' inner functions now don't
- all 1,256 JS/TS related tests pass
- full test suite: 8,422 passed. The 8 that fail (7 in `test_ext_tagged_id_clash.py`, 1 in `test_skill_no_backtick_substitution.py`) fail the same way on `v8` without this change, they need the SQL parser which my local setup doesn't have

## Not in this one

- in the import example, `a()` also gets a `calls lib_helper` link from the separate import pass, which doesn't know about inner functions. That's on `v8` too, so I left it for now
- inner functions written as `const helper = () => {}` still don't get nodes at all (#2143). I have that fix ready and will open it after this one, since it builds on this

Every Swift file that imports a module (`import Foundation`) mints the same module node id by design, and the extractors already exempt module and namespace nodes from collision disambiguation. `deduplicate_entities` still reported each such group as a lost-node ID collision, so a build printed one spurious `WARNING: node '...' is minted by two different files` for every extra importing file.
